identity.description: The Silent is a nimble assassin who excels at Poison damage, Shiv attacks, and the unique Sly/discard mechanic. The Silent has the best defensive tools in the game (Footwork, Blur, After Image, Wraith Form) and multiple distinct ways to scale damage. The Silent rewards careful, patient play — setting up defenses while slowly poisoning or chipping enemies to death.
identity.playstyle: Defensive setup into scaling damage. The Silent wants to establish defensive buffs (Footwork, Blur, After Image) early, then kill enemies with Poison stacking, Shiv spam, or Sly-powered discard combos. The starting relic rewards building a deck with a strong opening turn.
strengths: Best defensive scaling in the game — Footwork, After Image, Blur, Wraith Form
Poison bypasses block and armor — deals damage regardless of enemy defenses
Sly mechanic creates free card plays from discarding — unique action economy
Excellent card draw and cycling — Acrobatics, Backflip, Adrenaline
Shivs provide cheap, numerous attacks that scale with Strength and Accuracy
weaknesses: Lower base damage than Ironclad — frontloaded damage can be lacking in Act 1
Poison is slow — it takes multiple turns to kill tough enemies
Shiv builds need specific support cards (Accuracy, Kunai, Shuriken) to scale properly
Starting deck is weaker than Ironclad's — Strikes and Defends have lower base values
Some strategies require multiple specific pieces to function well

strikes.note: Remove as quickly as possible — Silent Strikes are the same as Ironclad's

defends.note: Remove after Strikes — slightly more Defends than Ironclad

neutralize.note: 0-cost with Weak application. Always play turn 1. Upgrade is high priority — 2 Weak is excellent.

survivor.note: Block + discard trigger. Excellent with Sly cards.

starting_relic.name: Ring of the Snake
starting_relic.effect: Draw 2 extra cards on turn 1 of each combat (7 card opening hand instead of 5)
starting_relic.strategic_value: A larger opening hand means more options on turn 1. You can play more cards, see more of your deck, and set up faster. This rewards having strong opening plays and synergies.
tips: Plan your turn 1 around having 7 cards — you can play more aggressively
Innate cards are extra valuable with Ring of the Snake — guaranteed in a larger hand
Discard effects on turn 1 are powerful — more cards in hand = more discard targets
The extra draw means you see 7/20 cards on turn 1 (35% of a 20-card deck) — very consistent

poison.description: Stack Poison on enemies to deal damage at the end of each turn. Poison ticks down by 1 each turn, so higher stacks deal more total damage. Catalyst doubles/triples Poison for burst damage.
core_cards: Deadly Poison — Apply 5/7 Poison. Simple, efficient, core Poison application.
Noxious Fumes — Apply 2/3 Poison to ALL enemies at start of each turn. Passive Poison scaling that's always good.
Catalyst — Double/Triple the enemy's Poison. The burst finisher — 20 Poison becomes 60 with upgraded Catalyst.
Crippling Cloud — Apply 4 Poison + 2 Weak to ALL enemies. AOE Poison + defensive utility.
Corpse Explosion — When an enemy dies, deal their max HP as damage to ALL enemies. AOE finisher.
support_cards: Poisoned Stab — 6/8 damage + apply 3/4 Poison. Attack + Poison in one card.
Envenom — whenever you deal unblocked attack damage, apply 1 Poison. Turns all attacks into Poison sources.
Bouncing Flask — Apply 3 Poison to random enemies 3/4 times. Multi-target Poison.
Bane — 7/10 damage. If enemy is Poisoned, deal 7/10 damage again (double hit). Payoff for Poison.
strengths: Poison bypasses enemy block — it deals damage regardless of defenses
Noxious Fumes provides passive scaling without needing to draw specific cards
Catalyst provides enormous burst damage potential (20 -> 60 -> 180 Poison)
Effective against high-block enemies and bosses with damage reduction
Doesn't require much energy — Poison cards are mostly 1-cost
weaknesses: Slow — Poison takes multiple turns to kill enemies, especially in Act 1
Weak against multiple enemies without Noxious Fumes or AOE Poison
Catalyst is all-or-nothing — amazing with high Poison stacks, useless without them
Enemy Artifact can prevent Poison application

shiv.description: Generate and play numerous Shiv cards (0-cost, 4 damage attacks) each turn. Scale Shiv damage with Accuracy (+damage per Shiv) and Strength. Play many attacks per turn for relic triggers (Kunai, Shuriken, etc.).
core_cards: Blade Dance — add 3/4 Shivs to your hand. The primary Shiv generator.
Cloak and Dagger — gain 6/8 block, add 1/2 Shivs to hand. Block + Shivs in one card.
Accuracy — Shivs deal +4/+6 damage. The primary Shiv scaling card.
Infinite Blades — gain 1 Shiv at start of each turn. Passive Shiv generation.
Storm of Steel — discard hand, gain 1 Shiv per card discarded. Massive Shiv burst.
support_cards: A Thousand Cuts — whenever you play a card, deal 1/2 damage to ALL enemies. Turns every Shiv into AOE chip damage.
After Image — whenever you play a card, gain 1 block. Turns every Shiv into +1 block.
Finisher — deal 6/8 damage per attack played this turn. Finisher after a Shiv-heavy turn.
Choke — deal 3/5 damage whenever enemy receives a card (from Shivs entering play). Unique scaling.
strengths: Huge number of attacks per turn — triggers attack-count relics (Kunai, Shuriken, Fan)
Shivs are 0-cost — they're free damage and free card plays
Scales with Accuracy, Strength, AND attack-count synergies simultaneously
After Image + many card plays = enormous block generation
Can deal very high total damage per turn with enough Shiv generation
weaknesses: Shivs are individually weak (4 damage) without Accuracy or Strength
Hand clogging — Shivs take up card slots in your hand, reducing options
Accuracy is essential but not always offered — Shiv builds without Accuracy are weak
Vulnerable to Time Eater (boss that punishes playing many cards per turn)
Shivs exhaust after being played — they're one-use
key_relic_synergies: Kunai — play 3 attacks, gain +1 Dexterity. Shivs trigger this easily.
Shuriken — play 3 attacks, gain +1 Strength. Makes Shivs hit harder.
Fan — play 3 attacks, gain 4 block. Free block from Shiv plays.
Ornamental Fan — same as Fan for some versions. Stacks with other attack-count relics.

sly_discard.description: Build around the Sly mechanic — cards that play themselves for free when discarded. Use discard effects (Acrobatics, Survivor, Gamble) to trigger Sly cards for massive action economy.
core_cards: Cards with Sly keyword — attacks and skills that trigger when discarded from hand
Acrobatics — draw 3/4, discard 1. The best discard trigger — draw AND trigger Sly.
Survivor — gain 8/11 block, discard 1. Block AND discard trigger.
Calculated Gamble — discard hand, draw that many. Mass discard triggers all Sly cards.
Tactician — discard to gain 1/2 energy. Energy generation from discarding.
support_cards: Reflex — cannot be played. When discarded, draw 2/3. Pure discard payoff.
Sneaky Strike — 12/16 damage. Costs 0 if you discarded a card this turn. Free damage with discard.
Concentrate — discard 3 cards, gain 2 energy. Mass discard with energy gain.
Tools of the Trade — at start of turn, draw 1 and discard 1. Passive discard trigger every turn.
strengths: Free card plays — Sly cards don't cost energy when triggered, creating insane action economy
Massive hand cycling — discard effects draw new cards while Sly cards play themselves
Combines well with both Poison and Shiv strategies
Very high ceiling — when the engine is running, you play 8+ cards per turn
Deck thinning through discard cycling improves consistency
weaknesses: Requires both Sly cards AND discard effects — missing either half is bad
Complex to pilot — sequencing matters enormously
Can misfire if you don't draw Sly cards and discard effects together
Calculated Gamble is risky — discarding your entire hand can backfire without Sly cards

cards.name: Wraith Form
cards.why: Gain 2/3 Intangible. All damage reduced to 1 for 2/3 turns. Best defensive card in the game.

cards.name: Adrenaline
cards.why: 0 cost. Gain 1/2 energy, draw 2/3 cards. Exhaust. Free energy and draw.

cards.name: Catalyst
cards.why: Double/Triple enemy Poison. Turns moderate Poison into lethal Poison.

cards.name: Corpse Explosion
cards.why: When enemy dies, deal their max HP to ALL enemies. AOE chain reaction.

cards.name: Noxious Fumes
cards.why: 2/3 Poison to ALL enemies every turn. Passive scaling that requires no further input.

tier_a.description: Almost always take. Very strong cards.

cards.name: Footwork
cards.why: +2/3 Dexterity permanently. Scales all your block cards. Multiple copies stack.

cards.name: Acrobatics
cards.why: Draw 3/4, discard 1. Excellent cycling and Sly trigger.

cards.name: Backflip
cards.why: Gain 5/8 block, draw 2. Block + draw in one card.

cards.name: Deadly Poison
cards.why: Apply 5/7 Poison. Simple, reliable Poison application.

cards.name: Dash
cards.why: 10/13 damage + 10/13 block. Replaces a Strike AND a Defend.

cards.name: After Image
cards.why: Gain 1 block every time you play a card. Insane with Shiv builds.

cards.name: Leg Sweep
cards.why: Apply 2/3 Weak + gain 11/14 block. Defensive powerhouse.

cards.name: Accuracy
cards.why: +4/+6 Shiv damage. Essential for Shiv builds.

cards.name: Blade Dance
cards.why: Add 3/4 Shivs to hand. Core Shiv generator.

cards.name: Predator
cards.why: 15/20 damage, draw 2 next turn. Frontload + future card draw.

cards.name: Backstab
cards.why: 0 cost, 11/15 damage, Innate, Exhaust. Free damage turn 1.

cards.name: Sucker Punch
cards.why: 7/9 damage + apply 1/2 Weak. Damage + defense in one card.

cards.name: Cloak and Dagger
cards.why: 6/8 block + add 1/2 Shivs. Block + Shivs.

cards.name: Blur
cards.why: Gain 5/8 block. Block doesn't expire next turn. Mini-Barricade for a turn.

cards.name: Malaise
cards.why: Apply X Weak + X Strength Down. Scales with energy. Devastating debuff.

cards.name: Tools of the Trade
cards.why: Draw 1, discard 1 at start of turn. Passive cycling and Sly trigger.

tier_c.description: Situational. Take only when they fill a specific need.

cards.name: Poisoned Stab
cards.why: 6/8 damage + 3/4 Poison. Jack of both trades, master of neither.

cards.name: Dagger Spray
cards.why: 4x2/6x2 damage to ALL enemies. Weak AOE but sometimes needed.

cards.name: Bouncing Flask
cards.why: Apply 3 Poison randomly 3/4 times. Inconsistent but fills Poison needs.

cards.name: Dodge and Roll
cards.why: 4/6 block this turn + 4/6 block next turn. Split block is awkward but can be useful.

cards.name: Prepared
cards.why: Draw 1/2, discard 1/2. 0-cost cycling and Sly trigger.

cards.name: Envenom
cards.why: Unblocked attacks apply 1 Poison. Good with Shivs but 2-cost Power is slow.

priorities: Upgrade Neutralize to apply 2 Weak — significant damage reduction from all enemies
Find frontloaded damage (Backstab, Predator, Dash) to handle hallway fights
Pick up Poison sources (Deadly Poison, Noxious Fumes) for scaling
Get at least 1 good block card beyond Defends (Backflip, Leg Sweep, Dash)
act1.card_priorities: Frontload damage > Poison/Scaling > Block cards > Card draw
act1.elite_readiness: Silent is slightly weaker in early Act 1 elites than Ironclad. Neutralize + Survivor help, but you may want an extra card or two before fighting elites.
act1.boss_preparation: Ensure you have Poison scaling (Noxious Fumes, Deadly Poison) or enough attacks to deal with the boss over a long fight.

priorities: Solidify your build direction — Poison, Shiv, or Sly/Discard
Add key Powers (Footwork, Noxious Fumes, After Image, Accuracy)
Upgrade scaling cards and key block cards
act2.elite_readiness: Your deck should handle elites if your strategy is coming together. Use Potions.
act2.boss_preparation: Wraith Form is the best boss card in the game — take it if offered. Ensure Poison or damage scaling is reliable.

priorities: Skip most card rewards — your deck should be built
Remove any filler cards at shops
Prepare specifically for the Act 3 boss
If offered Wraith Form and you don't have it, strongly consider taking it
act3.card_priorities: Only take cards that directly address a specific weakness.
act3.focus: Optimization. Catalyst upgrade (double -> triple) is one of the most powerful upgrades in the game if you have Poison.

common_pitfalls.slow_act1: Silent can struggle in Act 1 without frontloaded damage. Don't ignore attacks in favor of Poison — you need to kill things NOW in hallway fights.
common_pitfalls.no_aoe: Silent has limited AOE options. Without Noxious Fumes, Corpse Explosion, or Dagger Spray, multi-enemy fights are very dangerous.
common_pitfalls.shivs_without_accuracy: Shiv builds without Accuracy or Strength are very weak. 4 damage per Shiv doesn't scale fast enough without buffs.
common_pitfalls.too_many_skills: Silent decks can end up with too many skills and not enough attacks. You still need to deal damage.
common_pitfalls.wraith_form_without_plan: Wraith Form gives Intangible but reduces Dexterity each turn. You need Artifact or a plan to end the fight before Dexterity loss kills your block.
common_pitfalls.catalyst_without_poison: Catalyst is amazing but useless without Poison. Don't take Catalyst if you have no Poison application.
common_pitfalls.ignoring_footwork: Footwork is one of the best cards in the game. +2/3 Dexterity permanently makes every block card significantly better. Don't skip it.
